subject: Scoping: subprocessor audit access + Art.28/30 processing ledger for NovaHealth POC
messages:
From: Arielle Cohen <arielle.cohen@novahealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: NovaHealth Legal <legal@novahealth.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:18:00 +0200
Subject: Request: subprocessor audit scope + DPIA evidence for POC

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the NovaHealth POC is moving into security review and our legal/DPO teams have a few asks so we can complete vendor risk approval. High-level requests below: 

1) Audit access: we need a short, time-boxed method for our auditor to validate subprocessor controls relevant to processing of health-adjacent data during the POC (2–3 day window). Please confirm whether you can provide:
   - read-only access to an artifacts bundle or a hosted view,
   - a named auditor account with MFA, or
   - a remote, recorded walkthrough with your infra/ops team.

2) Art. 28/30 outputs: a machine-readable export of the processing activities ledger (Art.30) scoped to the POC dataset, plus a current subprocessor inventory that includes countries of processing and legal transfer mechanisms.

3) DPIA support: a short summary showing residual risk for the POC, and evidence of measures (encryption at rest/in transit, access logging, retention defaults).

We prefer electronic delivery (SFTP or secure Drive link) and redaction of customer PII before delivery. Can you confirm what you can provide and an estimated timeline? Ideally we’d have records by next Thursday (2027-06-24).

Best,
Arielle Cohen
Vendor Risk Manager
NovaHealth
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Arielle Cohen <arielle.cohen@novahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 11:02:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Request: subprocessor audit scope + DPIA evidence for POC

Hi Arielle —

Appreciate the clear list. Short answer: yes, we can meet these requests for the POC scope with a combination of artifacts and a time-boxed remote review. Proposed approach: 

- We’ll prepare an Art.28/30 ledger export scoped to the POC (csv) and a subprocessor inventory spreadsheet.
- For audit access we can either provide a named auditor account (read-only, MFA enforced) or a recorded remote walkthrough with infra logs exported; preference is the named account for direct verification.
- DPIA support: we’ll attach a 2-page summary that maps the POC processing flow to mitigations and residual risk.

I’ve looped in Marissa (Privacy & Compliance) to coordinate artifacts and Laura (Legal) for any redline/contract items. We can target delivery of the exports and DPIA summary by 2027-06-22 EOD CET and provision a 48-hour auditor access window the week of 2027-06-28 if that works for NovaHealth.

What format do you prefer for the ledger export (CSV schema preferred) and how will your auditor authenticate (SAML/IdP, temporary account)?

Thanks,
Sean Gallagher
Head of Sales 
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Arielle Cohen <arielle.cohen@novahealth.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:15:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Request: subprocessor audit scope + DPIA evidence for POC

Hi Arielle,

We’ll produce the artifacts listed and are aiming to keep delivery compact and machine-readable. A few details and asks from our side so we scope correctly: 

- Ledger schema: we will output a CSV with columns: processor_name, activity_description, legal_basis, categories_of_data, recipient_countries, transfer_mechanism, retention_default_days, last_reviewed. Please confirm if you need additional fields.
- Subprocessor inventory: current snapshot (includes onboarding date, country, subprocessors’ self-attestation of SOC2/ISO where available).
- Redaction: we will redact customer PII by default; if your auditor requires raw records for sampling we’ll need an executed data handling agreement and an SSO method.
- Audit methods supported: 1) temporary auditor account tied to a short-lived org role (preferred), 2) presigned S3 bundle (for artifacts), or 3) remote session with ops and recorded transcript.

Attachments I’ll push shortly: redwood-art28-30-ledger-20270620.csv (sample), subprocessor-inventory-20270620.xlsx, and a DPIA summary PDF for the POC. We will also include a short readme describing the ledger columns.

If NovaHealth can confirm the auditor identity and preferred authentication, we’ll provision the account and send credentials instructions.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment stubs: redwood-art28-30-ledger-20270620.csv (csv, 28KB); subprocessor-inventory-20270620.xlsx (xlsx, 45KB); dpia-summary-novahealth-POC.pdf (pdf, 2 pages)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Arielle Cohen <arielle.cohen@novahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 14:37:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Request: subprocessor audit scope + DPIA evidence for POC

Arielle —

Technical notes on delivery and sampling: 

- Export: attached CSV is a scoped extract (POC tag). Sample fields and a short mapping file are included in the Drive link below. We can also provide a JSON export if your tooling prefers.
- Access: for the auditor account we support SAML IdP federation (SAML2) or a short-lived local account. If NovaHealth can provide an SP metadata endpoint we’ll federate and issue a role scoped to read-only auditor privileges for N days.
- Logs and evidence: we’ll include the last 90 days of access logs relevant to POC resources (redacted IPs on request).
- Retention baseline: default retention for ephemeral POC artifacts is 30 days unless contractually extended.

Drive (artifact) link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1xExampleLedgerLink

If federation is not possible, we’ll create named credentials and deliver via secure vault (one-time retrieval) and rotate after the window. Please advise auditor email for provisioning.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Ops Engineer, Inference Platform
Redwood Inference
From: Arielle Cohen <arielle.cohen@novahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, NovaHealth Legal <legal@novahealth.com>, DPO Team <dpo@novahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 16:45:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Request: subprocessor audit scope + DPIA evidence for POC

Hi Marissa/Karthik —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and clear options. We reviewed the sample CSV and DPIA summary and they look good. A few confirmations: 

- Auditor: we will use an external firm (MediTrust Audit LLP). Auditor contact: Daniel Park (daniel.park@meditrust-llp.com). Please provision a scoped auditor account via SAML if possible; otherwise provide named credentials and we’ll coordinate retrieval.
- Delivery: Drive link is fine for artifacts; please redact any NovaHealth customer identifiers.
- Timeline: we confirm the requested artifacts by 2027-06-22 are acceptable and would like the audit window between 2027-06-28 and 2027-06-30.

Next steps: Sean — please confirm we have an assigned Redwood point of contact during the window (ops/infra) for live Q&A. Marissa/Karthik — please send the final artifacts and the provisioning instructions for the auditor.

I’ll loop in legal to prepare a brief NDA/data-handling addendum for the auditor access.

Best,
Arielle Cohen
Vendor Risk Manager
NovaHealth
